HealthOmics stages S3 directory URIs (with trailing slash) as a single mounted directory, but the wf-common xam_ingress sub-workflow's file()/Channel.fromPath() calls fail to enumerate BAM files inside that mount. Attempt 3 switches to explicit glob pattern URIs (*.bam) which HealthOmics stages by enumerating and materializing each matching S3 object as an individual file — this satisfies xam_ingress's expectation.

Glob-pattern URIs stage as a LinkedList of files, but main.nf does file(params.bam_tumor).exists() which requires a single Path, not a list. The pipeline fundamentally requires bam_tumor/bam_normal to each be a SINGLE file (or a real local directory on-prem). Neither S3 directory URIs nor S3 glob URIs work on HealthOmics. Resolution: pre-merge the two tumor BAMs into one sorted BAM and pass single-file URIs.

AWS HealthOmics stages S3 inputs differently (each parameter maps to a single staged file), so the directory-ingress path that works on-prem does not work on HealthOmics. Pre-merging is the HealthOmics-compatible equivalent.

cloud12_depth_aware.approach: User chose depth-aware split. New process split_candidates_by_depth (modules/local/wf-clair3-snp.nf): samtools bedcov on the phased BAM to get per-candidate coverage, then contiguous split by cumulative MEAN-DEPTH^2 budget (cost scales super-linearly with depth ~ depth^2, so coverage^1 under-corrects ~30x; depth^2 balances). Deep loci fragment into many small shards, shallow stay coarse -> balanced runtimes, no straggler, contiguous (no scatter penalty), accuracy-preserving. Wired: create_candidates(stock) -> candidate_beds_raw -> combine w/ phased_bam by [meta,ctg] -> split_candidates_by_depth -> flatMap -> evaluate_candidates. Param clairs_depth_split_budget=72000000 (mean_depth^2 units, TUNABLE - first run calibrates).
